issues.description: README diff drifts far beyond the PR's stated scope.
issues.detail: The PR claims to add POST tests and a small example fix, but the README diff reformats unrelated code, swaps str+reason for code_to_http_status, reorders handle() args, and switches to bounded_stream throughout. That is three separate changes smuggled into one review. Split it: scope is a data structure too.

issues.description: FAQ example conflates two read paths and obscures the actual lesson.
issues.detail: The lesson is 'how to set headers in tests'. The PostTest resource layers Content-Length checks, a conditional read, and three status codes to demonstrate it. Strip it: one handler that reads stream and returns 400 on empty body, one test that sets Content-Length. The data flow becomes obvious.

issues.description: bounded_stream swap in example is unexplained and behaviorally different.
issues.detail: Changing req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read() is the actual semantic fix that makes the new 400 test pass, yet it gets one line and no comment. The PR description says 'add req.content_length to req.stream.read()' which is not what the diff does. Name the change; document why bounded_stream is correct here.

issues.description: Test cases repeat header dict structure instead of composing.
issues.detail: resp3 and resp4 share Authorization and Content-Type. A small base headers dict merged with the per-case override would make the one meaningful difference (Content-Length: 1, empty body) jump out. Right data shape, obvious algorithm.

issues.description: FAQ test uses assert as a function call.
issues.detail: `assert(result.status == falcon.HTTP_400)` parses as assert on a tuple-less expression but reads like a function call and is a known pytest footgun pattern. Write `assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400`. Small thing, but FAQ code gets copied.

review.summary: The actual change here is small and reasonable: two new POST tests plus a bounded_stream fix in the example. The problem is scope. The README diff is a sweeping reformat plus semantic changes (handle signature, status construction, bounded_stream) that belong in a separate PR. The FAQ example is more elaborate than the lesson it teaches. Strip the README changes out, simplify the FAQ resource to the smallest thing that demonstrates the point, and call out the bounded_stream swap explicitly.
